name: Cyrus Cylinder
evidence: Records Cyrus’s conquest and restoration policies.
limits: Does not name the Jewish return or describe Belshazzar’s feast.
credit: Mike Peel (www.mikepeel.net); modifications credited to مانفی

name: Tel Dan Stele
evidence: Aramaic inscription widely read as referring to the House of David.
limits: Does not establish all details of David’s life; royal claims require critical comparison.

name: Lachish siege relief
date: Early 7th century BCE; campaign conventionally dated 701 BCE
evidence: Assyrian palace carvings commemorate the capture of Lachish.
limits: Royal propaganda; does not independently establish the outcome at Jerusalem.

name: Pilate inscription
evidence: Latin inscription names Pontius Pilate and his office as prefect of Judaea.
limits: Does not independently document Jesus’ trial. Photo is a modern copy at Caesarea.

name: Great Isaiah Scroll
evidence: Ancient Hebrew copy containing the entire book of Isaiah.
limits: Evidence for textual transmission, not independent verification of each narrated event.
